SOURCE: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/spark-ui-guide/slow-spark-stage-low-io
FETCHED: 2026-06-17
PART OF: Spark UI Guide series (Step 5 of 5)

=== DIAGNOSTIC APPROACH ===
Navigate to the job page → click "Associated SQL Query" at top → SQL DAG opens.
"these times are cumulative, so it's the total time spent on all the tasks, not the clock time."
Some nodes show timing directly (e.g. "2.1 minutes"); others require expansion to reveal duration (e.g. "1.4 minutes").
Timing in DAG correlates with clock time and cost.

=== CAUSE 1: READING MANY SMALL FILES ===
"If you're reading tens of thousands of files or more, you may have a small file problem. Your files should be no less than 8MB."
Root cause: "most often caused by partitioning on too many columns or a high-cardinality column."
Examine scan operator details for file counts.

Remediation:
- Execute OPTIMIZE command → https://docs.databricks.com/en/sql/language-manual/delta-optimize.html
- Enable predictive optimization → /aws/en/optimizations/predictive-optimization
- Reconsider file layout → databricks.com/discover/pages/optimize-data-workloads-guide#data-layout

=== CAUSE 2: WRITING MANY SMALL FILES ===
"If you're writing tens of thousands of files or more, you may have a small file problem. Your files should be no less than 8MB."
Root cause: "partitioning on too many columns or a high-cardinality column."
Review write operation details for file count and data volume.

Remediation:
- Enable predictive optimization
- Reconsider file layout
- Activate optimized writes

=== CAUSE 3: SLOW UDFs ===
"If you think you're suffering from this problem, try commenting out your UDF to see how it impacts the speed of your pipeline."
"If the UDF is indeed where the time is being spent, your best bet is to rewrite the UDF using native functions."

Parallelization fix:
"If it's less than the number of cores on your cluster, repartition() your dataframe before using the UDF."

Code:
  (df
    .repartition(num_cores)
    .withColumn('new_col', udf(...))
  )

Memory fix:
"Each task may have to load all the data in its partition into memory. If this data is too big, things can get very slow or unstable. Repartition also can resolve this issue by making each task smaller."

NOTE: UDF node image is a base64 data URI on this page — not downloadable as standalone file.

=== CAUSE 4: CARTESIAN JOIN ===
"If you see a cartesian join or nested loop join in your DAG, you should know that these joins are very expensive."

=== CAUSE 5: EXPLODING JOIN / EXPLODE ===
"If you see a few rows going into a node and magnitudes more coming out, you may be suffering from an exploding join or explode()."
Reference: databricks.com/discover/pages/optimize-data-workloads-guide#data-explosion
